bug_semantics: Authenticated compose-mail (POST /admin/mail/create) accepts arbitrary attachments with no extension or executable-type check. EmailRepository::create always calls AttachmentRepository::uploadAttachments. At v2.1.5, prepareData() writes the client original filename onto the default public disk as emails/<email_id>/<original_name> via Storage::put. Attachment::url() returns Storage::url() under APP_URL/storage (public disk root storage/app/public, symlink public/storage), so an uploaded test.php is reachable as /storage/emails/<id>/test.php and executed by the web server (unrestricted upload leading to CWE-94 RCE). EmailController store() only validates reply_to/reply.
flaw_origin: c42bad26269130aed2ef25ae4959b956fc754485 (Suraj Kashyap, 2025-05-09, 'fix: resolve attachment display issue and TinyMCE editor visibility') first wrote prepareData() storing web compose uploads as emails/<id>/<getClientOriginalName()> on the default public disk. Immediate parent 56ee80d9 still used UploadedFile::store('emails/'.$email->id), which hashes the on-disk name. That original-name public put is the BIC for the published PoC path; it is an ancestor of v2.1.5 and the AttachmentRepository file is byte-identical in v2.1.6. deae55ce later split IMAP vs UploadedFile but kept the same original-name put. Filename neutralization (DANGEROUS_EXTENSIONS + sanitizeName appending .txt) first appears in ea4919a8, first tagged v2.2.5; 4d818957 then moved new attachments to the private local disk. The advisory first_patched_version 2.1.6 does not match the tree: v2.1.5..v2.1.6 has no AttachmentRepository/filesystems.php change and SanitizeFileUploads.php is absent at v2.1.6.
ai_marker: absent; BIC author/committer are both Suraj Kashyap <suraj.kashyap370@webkul.in>; git cat-file -p shows a GPG signature and the human message 'fix: resolve attachment display issue and TinyMCE editor visibility' with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or bot author.

reasoning: Vulnerability first: the published issue is real unrestricted attachment upload on compose-mail that lands a client-named .php file on the public disk and executes it. It is not withdrawn. The v2.1.5 sink is prepareData()'s original-name public put, not the 2.1.6 XSS/URL middleware work. BIC: the smallest commit that first wrote those original-name public-put lines is c42bad26; the parent still hashed names via store(), so this is not a move of identical lines. c6a050ea earlier introduced public-disk attachment storage without type checks, but web uploads used hashed names and are not the 2.1.5/PoC lines. c42bad26 is a single-parent non-merge, not a squash. AI second: judge only the BIC object — human Webkul author/committer, GPG signature, no AI trailer or bot identity — therefore NOT_AI. Fix: advisory 2.1.6 does not close the sink (identical AttachmentRepository; no upload sanitizer). The first mechanism-closing commit in public history is ea4919a8 (neutralize dangerous extensions, including php, before writing on the public disk), first released in v2.2.5.
